purpose: Repeatable local diagnostics plus separate human review of real, owned or licensed speech clips.
syntheticLimit: Generated patterns and tones test technical behavior only. They do not validate speech recognition, semantic B-roll relevance, editorial quality, or platform treatment.

humanCases.audience: People who keep checking work messages after hours
humanCases.intendedTakeaway: Writing down the next action before closing the laptop can make it easier to leave work for the evening.

authoredSpeech.before: My workday ended at six, but I kept checking messages all evening.
authoredSpeech.focus: I couldn't switch off after work.
authoredSpeech.after: I now write down the first task for tomorrow, then close the laptop. This routine helped me stop reopening it during dinner.

stockPair.visualIntent: Person working late at a laptop, then closing the laptop or writing a short task list.
stockPair.portraitRequirement: The hands and laptop action remain visible after the selected crop.

humanChecks: The visual depicts finishing work rather than a literal electrical switch.
The opening identifies work messages or the evening routine without requiring an earlier sentence.
The edit delivers one personal example and ends with the complete practical takeaway.
The speaker's personal experience is not rewritten as a proven benefit for everyone.

humanCases.audience: People comparing paper and phone task lists
humanCases.topic: A practical comparison of two task-list methods
humanCases.intendedTakeaway: Paper helped this speaker avoid notifications; a phone list was easier to carry.

authoredSpeech.before: J'ai comparé une liste de tâches sur mon téléphone et une liste sur papier pendant une semaine.
authoredSpeech.focus: Avec celle-ci, je ne me laissais plus distraire par les notifications.
authoredSpeech.after: Je parle de la liste sur papier. Le téléphone était plus pratique en déplacement, mais le carnet m'aidait à rester concentré à mon bureau.

stockPair.visualIntent: A hand writing a task list in a paper notebook; a distinct phone-list shot can illustrate the comparison.
reject: generic phone scrolling used to illustrate the paper-list benefit
stockPair.portraitRequirement: Keep the writing hand and notebook in the portrait frame.

humanChecks: Neighboring sentences resolve celle-ci to the paper list.
English stock queries describe visible action despite French speech.
The opening names both compared methods instead of starting with an unexplained pronoun.
The ending preserves the phone's practical benefit as well as the notebook's benefit.
Captions preserve the spoken French meaning and the speaker's qualification.

humanCases.audience: Creators evaluating a simple workspace demonstration
humanCases.intendedTakeaway: Labels helped identify cables in one demonstration; distinguish that observation from a universal claim.

authoredSpeech.before: In this example I am discussing my collaborator Alex's cable-labeling demonstration, used with their permission.
authoredSpeech.focus: Alex labeled the two charger cables before putting them back behind the desk. They then picked the requested cable without unplugging the other one.
authoredSpeech.after: My takeaway is to label cables before routing them. This is one demonstration, not a measured time-saving study. Alex made the original demonstration; I added the comparison with my own unlabeled setup.

stockPair.visualIntent: Hands placing a label on a cable, identified as illustrative footage if it is not the original demonstration.
reject: stock footage presented as the actual cited demonstration
stockPair.portraitRequirement: The label and the cable receiving it remain visible.

humanChecks: Use this authored scenario after recording a real demonstration with permission; replace Alex with the actual credited creator.
The selected excerpt contains the observed example and the speaker's own explanation.
The ending retains the limitation that this is one demonstration.
Original creator/source credit remains visible or audible in the export and recorded in source notes.
Illustrative stock footage is not represented as evidence from the original demonstration.

reviewRubric.brollAcceptance: Count accepted shots over all proposed shots; also record no-match moments and incorrect no-match decisions.
reviewRubric.captionCorrections: Count caption cues changed after the first proposal; note recurring names, numbers, language and timing errors.
reviewRubric.opening: pass: a new viewer can identify the subject and claim; needs-work: important context or a pronoun is unexplained; not-reviewed: no judgment yet.
reviewRubric.ending: pass: the idea and necessary qualifications finish completely; needs-work: the conclusion is clipped or changes the source's meaning; not-reviewed: no judgment yet.
reviewRubric.attribution: Identify the actual creator/source and permission; preserve attribution and distinguish source evidence from illustrative stock.
reviewRubric.distinctIdea: Write one sentence describing this version's useful example, analysis, comparison or demonstration; a new headline alone does not supply a new idea.
reviewRubric.correctionTime: Time active corrections from first preview until acceptance, in minutes; exclude unattended rendering time.
reviewRubric.postPublication: If posted, record the actual platform, measurement date, watch time, completion, saves, shares and exact platform notices. Compare similar audience, duration and observation periods; leave unavailable metrics blank.
